scope: Native verification of material registration, random-flask enumeration, terrain color lookup and creation mechanisms in the pinned unmodified Noita executable. Static analysis; no game execution.

inheritance.finding: CellData constructs defaults before XML overlay. CellDataChild copies the resolved parent, including these flags, before overlaying attributes. Attribute absence preserves the previous value.

flaskEnumeration.creationBoundary: Enumeration itself creates no material. The shipped random-flask Lua script chooses only the liquid/sand lists with include_statics=false. Runtime fungal conversions can change record properties; the audited pool describes the initial registry.

factoryLookup.match: first matching runtime material ID in ascending order; ID0's special color checked first

bitmapLookup.match: first matching color-vector index; input and entries are RGB-masked

fixedBitmap.finding: Fixed-bitmap biome sampling checks RGB and resolves the color without testing alpha; it must not inherit the Wang transparent-pixel exclusion.

materialOverrides.finding: LoadPixelScene color_to_material_table keys are explicitly masked to RGB; values are looked up as material names.

terrainColorLookup.limitation: Image-role reachability must be established from game sources. A visual color match does not establish material placement. The duplicate-color outcome depends on actual runtime registration order.

registryTags.finding: These tag-map memberships do not exclude statics or particle-only materials; they are distinct from the filtered flask enumerations.

fungal_shift_particle_fx.finding: Material finalization writes each owner's material ID into ParticleEffect.m_material_id(+4); fungal_shift_particle_fx owns ID223. Fungal conversion copies this effect including ID223 into converted definitions. World-cell rendering queues the copied effect pointer from CellData+0x28c; the queue drains into cosmetic emission using m_material_id. Thus converted cells can emit cosmetic particles of fungal_shift_particle_fx even though the definition is not used for normal terrain cells.
fungal_shift_particle_fx.sourceFinding: The comment that only its particle effect is used describes this actual cosmetic use; it is not a basis for an unused-content exclusion.

concrete_collapsed.finding: LooseGroundSystem passes chunk_material to its collapse helper. Zero selects concrete_collapsed, and selected terrain pixels are replaced by a physics body of that material. Needs a reachable component with chunk_probability > 0 and default chunk_material to prove gameplay availability.

wood_loose.finding: PixelSprite constructor sets wood_loose through PixelSprite::SetMaterial; the setter stores its resolved ID at +0xf4. Needs reachable PixelSprite creation that preserves the default to establish this specific material.

aluminium.finding: Native references set IKLimb/IKLimbWalker ray_skip_material; shipped component docs say this material is excluded from ray casting. This reference does not create aluminium.

radioactive_gas_static.finding: The effect path assigns material damage zero and rebuilds DamageModel material-damage vectors/strings; it does not create cells. Other sources may create the material.

gold_static_radioactive.finding: The effect path assigns material damage zero and rebuilds DamageModel material-damage vectors/strings; it does not create cells.

glass.finding: Earlier byte-search hits were substrings of ice_radioactive_glass and explosions/magic_glass_cannon, not exact glass material literals.

rainbow_gas.finding: RAINBOW_FARTS maps to effect enum0x5c at0x690f9e–0x690fae. Game-effect update0xb015d0 handles case0x5c, locates ParticleEmitterComponent tagged fart and periodically writes its is_emitting flag at+0x108. This activates the initially disabled rainbow_gas emitter in the shipped effect entity.
rainbow_gas.sourceFinding: GameEffectComponent uses RAINBOW_FARTS; ParticleEmitterComponent tagged fart declares emitted_material_name=rainbow_gas and is_emitting=0. The native updater supplies the activation route.
rainbow_gas.limitation: Activation timing is statically inspected; no runtime spawning was performed.

spark_player.finding: The native player-disappearance helper loads the facing-specific effect entity; these entities emit spark_player. One caller is gated by a debug-related global initialized to zero; another requires co-op world mode and another registered player. The exact normal controller/player-lifecycle reach of that second branch remains unverified.

debugFlag.referenceKinds: all21 recovered exact references read the byte; no exact byte-address write or pointer registration found

spark_player.concreteGap: Controller switching can mark an entity for later deletion (0x44df60) while registered-player handles are maintained separately. The audit has not established that transient player-count/co-op states can never reach the disappearance branch during normal hardware/respawn timing.
spark_player.exclusionDecision: Keep visible; neither positive normal-gameplay use nor unused status is certified.

freshGridCells.resolvedConstructorCallers: Each constructor has only 0x7048c0 as a resolved direct caller.
freshGridCells.finding: The factory consumes a supplied material definition. The numeric adapter validates and indexes a supplied ID; these helpers perform no arbitrary-registry random selection.

worldGeneration.finding: Reviewed cores use configured biome-band material pointers, RGB-to-ID image maps, or existing material IDs in cached chunk data. Noise chooses among configured bands, not arbitrary registry IDs.

cosmeticParticles.finding: All28 resolved direct caller functions were inspected. They reduce to source material fields, fixed named materials, previously existing cell/inventory/stain IDs or ParticleEffect owner IDs. Cosmetic use counts as use; the copied fungal ParticleEffect is an affirmative counterexample to declaring its owner unused.

solidBodies.finding: Bulk body placement consumes an existing supplied per-pixel material-ID map; PhysicsAddBodyImage resolves image RGB; PixelSprite activation0xbedab0 resolves component.material(+0x68), with default wood_loose. LooseGround uses source chunk_material or fixed concrete_collapsed. Body builder0x91ea30 reads optional material density/friction/restitution/gravity only; null uses physics constants rather than choosing a material. Body-to-grid conversion0x720960 preserves existing cell definitions unless supplied an explicit conversion ID.
solidBodies.decompilerLimitation: 0x91ea30 pseudocode loses its tail after a mistaken no-return assumption. The complete relevant assembly is retained as physics-body-create.asm and was used for the property/default finding.

explosions.finding: Initial creation IDs are name lookups of create_cell_material/spark_material. Real sparks use spark_material when material_sparks_real is enabled. Destroyed-cell replacement can use its configured solid_on_collision_material; fallback dirt is the fixed explosion_dirt definition. Debris can copy the existing cell or PixelSprite material. No registry-wide choice or material-name suffix generation occurs in the reviewed explosion routine.

ragdollParticles.origin: DamageModelComponent.ragdoll_material (+0x144, default meat), or active GameEffectComponent.ragdoll_material (+0x74, default0) override. KillMe resolves the name, captures its ID, and forwards it unchanged to the image-particle callback.

gameEffect.finding: These reviewed game-effect update/attachment handlers do not assign a new material to the GameEffect +0x74 ragdoll override.

phaseChanges.finding: Loading cold_freezes_to_material_name writes its resolved ID to +0x148. Unless disableReverse is set, it also writes the source material ID to the frozen target's warmTarget(+0x144). The resolver subsequently resolves or clears each record's own warm target in registry order. Runtime heat/freezing conversion reads these resolved fields; this path does not consult an additional reverse-transition table.
phaseChanges.sourceJoin: Use final resolved runtime warmth_melts_to_material and cold_freezes_to_material_id, not just XML attribute text, so generated reverse edges are included.

certificationBoundary.confirmed: Listed53 source candidates have no surviving concrete initial-seed route in the reviewed native production families after the explicit source-domain joins. This file remains a native mechanism review; the final per-material exclusion certificate must also bind the matching source/validation evidence and executable/data digests.
remaining: spark_player: native disappearance entities are proven, but normal controller/respawn reach of the co-op branch remains unverified; keep it visible.
certificationBoundary.notAProof: Absence of a literal material name and the existence of generic debug/mod spawning APIs are neither sufficient unused proofs nor gameplay creation routes.

variantNameReview.scope: Material registration/name lookup, the reviewed worldgen/physics/conversion/explosion producers and whole-file suffix-literal counterexample search.
variantNameReview.finding: No independent material-name variant generator was identified in these native creation paths. Physics shape creation retains source material definitions rather than deriving a vertical-name variant from orientation. convert_to_box2d_material and solid_break_to_type are explicit source fields at +0x1ec/+0x1d0. Reaction tag/suffix transformations are supplied by materials.xml and must be expanded against their bound input names.
variantNameReview.literalSearch: _molten, _part2 and _trailer have no binary text hit. _vertical only occurs in do_only_vertical_stripe. _box2d appears in configuration/type labels and convert_to_box2d_material. Literal absence is supporting evidence only.

boundedImmediateScan.limitation: Only decoded indirect slot0x20 calls with literal or nearest register-immediate IDs in the x86 placement argument position; not a complete dataflow proof.

normalCreationClosure.scope: Original material definitions in the pinned unmodified game, including cosmetic use and official Nightmare content; developer/mod inputs and hypothetical arbitrary API calls are not normal-gameplay seed routes.
normalCreationClosure.basis: All concrete ID-origin questions found in the reviewed normal producer families reduce to source-resolved fields/defaults, source-selected images, explicit native named materials, runtime-resolved phase/reaction targets or a copy of an already existing material. The separate source review closes those input domains for these53 candidates.

families.proof: Native type/static/particle predicates and ID0 exclusion, joined to shipped chest/potion scripts.
Configured biome-band definitions and RGB image maps; source review includes native exact-path roots, remaps, fixed-bitmap alpha behavior, spliced images and native effect filenames.
Recovered central constructors/factory callers and9 actual-material-particle caller functions; output IDs derive from source fields, fixed names, existing inventories/cells, or resolved transitions.
All28 resolved cosmetic-creator caller functions inspected; named/configured IDs, existing cells/stains/inventories, and ParticleEffect owner IDs. Borrowed fungal effect remains explicitly used.
Image/PixelSprite material maps, fixed/default wood_loose/concrete_collapsed, DamageModel/GameEffect ragdoll material fields; body core supplies physics properties only.
Explicit convert_to_box2d_material/solid_break_to_type fields and source-bound reaction suffixes; no independent rotation-based material-name generator found in reviewed body/conversion code.
Animal polymorph registry filters _physics names; entity/gfx preloading does not instantiate world material; native effect_ and spliced prefix domains cross-joined by source reviewer.

explicitExceptions.fungal_shift_particle_fx: Verified cosmetic use after borrowed ParticleEffect copy; excluded from unused candidates.
explicitExceptions.rainbow_gas: Verified native activation of shipped fart-tagged emitter; used.
explicitExceptions.spark_player: Native player-disappearance entities exist, but their debug/co-op reach is still being reviewed; excluded from this closure until resolved.

limitations: This is an evidence-bounded source/native mechanism review, not a formal proof over all possible executable paths.
The378 syntactic virtual-slot calls are a separate supporting immediate-ID check, not a complete native virtual-call graph.
No current gameplay session or material API runtime dump was executed.

nativeAssetReferences.finding: All exact references were offered to source review as candidate roots rather than automatically treated as world spawns. Only spark_player's native disappearance entities introduced a remaining conditional candidate producer.

polymorph.finding: The normal pool removes blacklist-substring entries. A separate named rare pool is constructed for listed monsters; _physics variants are not moved into that rare pool. The concrete boss_limbs_physics aluminium candidates are excluded.

preloading.finding: Entity/gfx directory sweeps are template/image preloading. The XML branch calls template retrieval, not entity/world-material construction.

effectPrefix.finding: Built from game-effect enum names; source review conservatively inspected every shipped effect_*.xml and dependencies.

splicedPrefix.finding: Source review checked every shipped spliced image, including transparent RGB values, for candidates.
